points: I want to digress for a minute, because there are a lot of you heathen that are watching us, or Gentiles that are watching us, and this comes up a lot when we say that the Bible is exclusive for the Israelites. They always bring up Rahab the harlot. So next time you all are in the street teaching and people bring up, what about Rahab — because in the New Testament they mention her faith, but they never say why they mention her faith.

And Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim two men to spy secretly, saying, Go view the land, even Jericho. And they went, and came into an harlot's house, named Rahab, and lodged there. Because they were going to take the land.
Joshua sent two men out of Shittim to spy secretly and view the land, even Jericho, and they came into the house of a harlot named Rahab and lodged there.

And the king of Jericho sent unto Rahab, saying, Bring forth the men that are come to thee, which are entered into thine house: for they be come to search out all the country. So the king said, I want those men, bring them to me.

The king of Jericho sent to Rahab for the men, and she hid them under the flax on the roof and sent the pursuers the wrong way: some brothers and sisters will be looked to to hide the prophets, and helping will put you in danger.

Word made its way to the king of Jericho that men of the children of Israel had come to search out the country, and he sent unto Rahab to bring them forth. She had taken the two men and hid them on the roof under the stalks of flax she had laid in order there.

The city shall be accursed, even it and all that are therein, to the Lord: only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers. She made a covenant with the spies: she would conceal them and assist Israel, knowing the Lord was with Israel, as long as her family was saved when the city fell.

Rahab is the scripture's own example that a man is justified by works and not by faith only: faith and works go hand in hand, for your actions prove whether you believe. Was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers and sent them out another way? As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

note.label: Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab

points: Joshua sent the two spies into the harlot's house to bring out Rahab and all that she had, as they sware unto her; they brought out her father, mother, brethren, and all her kindred, and left them without the camp of Israel.

note.label: Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab

points: Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive and her father's household, and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day, because she hid the messengers. She helped the nation of Israel toward rulership, and that is the only help Israel wants from the other nations: not food stamps, welfare, or reparations, but tell our people who they are, the Israelites the Bible speaks of, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, and that we must keep the commandments of the Most High. Whoever does that will receive mercy just as Rahab did.

note.label: Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab

points: Generation goes back to genes and genealogy: Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar, Phares begat Esrom, down to Naasson, Salmon, Booz of Rachab, Obed of Ruth, Jesse and David the king.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac; faith wrought with his works and by works was faith made perfect, and he was called the friend of God. By works a man is justified and not by faith only, as Romans 2:13 said, and Rahab was justified by works when she sent the spies out another way. As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.
